answer: Each agent identity holds a willow: a hash-chained work history in a shared vault, where every completed task commits the identity's next nonce. The chain is linear by protocol, so an attacker cannot fork one reputation into parallel copies — any fork reuses a spent nonce and is rejected on its first job. New identities start weightless and must finish priced, audited work before earning voting or payment rights, so a sybil attack means buying genuine labor at scale for each fake agent, plus a marble-verification deposit that is slashed when duplicate nonces surface.
